The default loop everywhere is now boot-based:

  diagnostic count on the wheel (and the grep learns the wheel's

  FROM_SEED=1 restores the seed-sparked path

  ASSERTED ON EVERY RUN — the fixpoint ratchet. Because boot is
  wheel-emitted, m2 == m3 IS the fixed point; the seed-era rule

  seed. --fixpoint extends one more generation; --from-seed walks
  the cold ladder (band J archaeology, diverse-double-compilation)

8/8 rungs + 52/52 micros through boot's wheel-emitted m2, and the
march prints 'FIXED POINT holds: m2 == m3' — a two-generation ratchet,
seed build and pass-1 gone from the hot path.

Three root causes, one round:

- Pattern-params desugar (SYNTAX.md:268 `((a, b)) => a + b` is canon):
  paren-contents parse as exprs; the TParam converter FABRICATED an
  empty-string name for any non-VarRef param (the $ident_at_p
  fabrication class), so tuple-param lambdas bound nothing. Now
  $lambda_params_normalize routes pattern-shaped params through a
  synthesized binder ('tp' + fresh handle — collision-proof) + a
  LetStmt(pat, binder) prepended to the body — pattern-param IS
  let-pattern sugar; the existing pattern substrate does the rest.
  Unblocks cursor.mn filter/map tuple lambdas + own.mn:73.

- $env_lookup_ctor (kind 132 only) for pattern-ctor position:
  types.mn `type Handle = Int where ...` (alias) shadowed
  threading.mn `type Handle = Handle(Int)` (ctor) — value-class
  filtering wasn't sharp enough for patterns, which are ctor-only.
  Retargets infer_walk_pat PCon + lower pat-ctor lookups.

- Wheel fixes: driver.mn `cache.hash_source(...)` module-qualified
  call -> bare (one namespace, one name); infer.mn append_one ->
  push (the snoc substrate), make_buffer(8) -> buf_make() (the
  buffer.mn maker), same_ground's TAlias arm called is_concrete —
  wrong fn, doesn't exist — now recurses same_ground(inner, b) so
  aliases compare transparently; threading.mn 'for now' comment
  rewritten to state what closure_done_addr does.

mentl/771b042:
The first compiler component written in Lux! std/compiler/lexer.lux can
tokenize Lux source code into a list of (type, value, line, col) tuples.

## New VM builtins (vm.rs + checker/builtins.rs):
  char_at, char_code, from_char_code, ends_with, index_of,
  string_slice, parse_float, to_int, type_of

## Self-hosted lexer (std/compiler/lexer.lux):
  - Character classification: is_digit, is_alpha, is_alnum, is_whitespace
  - Table-driven keyword lookup (22 keywords)
  - Table-driven two-char operator lookup (10 operators)
  - Char-code-based single-char token dispatch (20 tokens)
  - scan_string with escape sequences (\n, \t, \\, \")
  - scan_number with float support (e.g. 3.14)
  - Line comment stripping (//)
  - Line/column tracking

## Lexer test suite (examples/lexer_test.lux):
  10 tests covering: char classification, keywords, simple expressions,
  strings, operators, functions, floats, comments, line tracking

## Discovered: VM closure capture bug
  Inner functions defined inside other functions dont properly capture
  parent scope variables after import resolution. Workaround: pass all
  state as explicit parameters instead of relying on closure capture.

All 37 Rust + 19 self + 10 lexer = 66 tests pass.
